ImageDescription.value:
C4A-04 POST-WAR CLASSIC (BRITISH & EUROPEAN)

Debuting at the 1954 New York Auto show, the 190SL was sold alongside the faster, more expensive Mercedes-Benz 300SL, which it closely resembled both in its styling and in its fully independent suspension, with both cars having double wishbone suspensions at the front and swing axles at the rear. However, the 190SL did not use the 300SL's purpose-built tubular space-frame W198 platform, and was instead built on the shortened monocoque R121 platform, which was modified from the W121 small saloon platform.

The car was available either as a soft top convertible or with removable hardtop. In its early life, the 190SL could also be had as a sports-racing model with small perspex windscreen and aluminum door. In 1959, the hardtop's rear window was enlarged.

The 190SL was also referred to as the Nitribitt-Mercedes after the 1957 scandal surrounding the murder of the call girl Rosemarie Nitribitt, who owned a 190SL.

This particular example was found gathering dust in a garage in Los Angeles in 2009. It is an original right-hand drive car imported to US from the UK before being imported into Australia.

ImageDescription.value:
The Mercedes-Benz 300SL was the first car in the SL-Class and it was the fastest production car of its day. Also available at the time was the cheaper 190SL. They shared basic styling, engineering, detailing, and fully independent suspension. While both cars had double wishbones in front and swing axles at the rear, the 190 SL did not use the 300 SL's purpose-built W198 tubular spaceframe. The 300SL was available from 1954-57 as a 2 seat sports car with distinctive gull-wing doors and later from 1958-63 as an open roadster. Both the 190 SL and the 300 SL were replaced by the Mercedes-Benz 230SL in 1963

Engine; 220hp 2996cc SOHC 6 cyl

The Mercedes Benz 190 SL was a 2 door luxury roadster built from 1955-63, a more affordable version of the 300SL. They shared basic styling, engineering, detailing, and fully independent suspension. While both cars had double wishbones in front and swing axles at the rear, the 190 SL did not use the 300 SL's purpose-built W198 tubular spaceframe. Instead, it was built on a shortened monocoque R121 platform modified from the W121 small saloon. The 190SL was available either as a soft-top convertible or with removable hardtop. Both the 190 SL and the 300 SL were replaced by the Mercedes-Benz 230SL in 1963

Engine; 104hp 1897cc SOHC 4 cyl
